notes: ZATCA: investment gold/silver (99%+, tradable on the global bullion market) is zero-rated; jewellery is taxed at 15% on the full sale price (guideline s5.2 worked example). Dealer figures dropped: Ounce's price and buy-back pages render no readable rates and the old ladder was built on zahabprice (banned); gold.sa's used-gold page carries only stale 2025 averages.

sources.name: ZATCA - Guideline for the Investment Metals Sector under VAT Provisions (Issue 2, May 2026)
sources.what: Qualified metals are gold, silver and platinum; a qualified metal supplied for investment purposes (purity not less than 99% and tradable on the international bullion market) is zero-rated (section 4); jewellery and precious articles are not investment-metal supplies and their sale is subject to VAT at the standard rate of 15%, applied on the sale price (section 5.2 and Example 7); the standard VAT rate is 15%.

sources.name: Common VAT Agreement of the GCC (hosted by ZATCA), Article 35
sources.what: Article 35: gold, silver or platinum is an investment metal when its purity is not less than 99% and it is tradable on the Global Bullion Exchange, and 'the supply of investment gold, silver and platinum shall be subject to the zero-rate'.

sources.name: PwC Tax Summaries - Saudi Arabia, Corporate - Other taxes
sources.what: VAT applied from 1 January 2018 and 'effective 1 July 2020, the standard VAT rate was increased by the government to 15%' - corroborates the 15% standard rate applied to jewellery.
